title: Akara (Bean Fritters)
description: Crisp, fluffy fritters of peeled black-eyed beans, onion and pepper — Saturday breakfast and roadside favourite, best with pap or bread.

image.alt: Pile of golden-brown akara bean fritters

ingredients.constraint: Use as little as possible or the akara won't hold

steps.instruction: Soak the beans in plenty of water.
Rub the beans between your palms to loosen the skins, then float the skins off with water. Repeat until white.

cues.visual: Beans white, with few skins left.

steps.instruction: Blend the peeled beans with the onion, scotch bonnets and just enough water to get the blades moving.

cues.texture: Thick and smooth — it holds its shape on a spoon.

steps.instruction: Beat the paste hard with a wooden spoon or whisk to work in air. Add salt just before frying.

cues.visual: Paler in colour and noticeably bigger in volume.

steps.instruction: Heat the oil in a deep pan.

cues.sound: A drop of batter sizzles and floats up immediately.

steps.safetyNote: Keep children away from the pan and never leave the oil unattended.

steps.instruction: Scoop tablespoons of batter into the oil and fry, turning, until golden brown all over. Fry in batches without crowding.
steps.safetyNote: Slide the batter in close to the oil — dropping it from high splashes.

image.alt: Akara frying in a wide pan of oil over an open fire

steps.instruction: Lift out and drain on kitchen paper. Serve hot.

notes: Don't salt the batter until you're ready to fry — salt draws out water and makes it runny.
Serve with pap (ogi or akamu), custard or soft white bread.
